title: Michael Dell, Intel co-founder Gordon Moore’s funds among 8 largest university gifts
content: Ken Griffin just made a huge splash in the world of philanthropy by donating a whopping $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University! This massive gift includes $2 billion for a cutting-edge campus in Miami and $1 billion for the prestigious School of Computer Science in Pittsburgh.

title: Washington farmer challenges $618,000 irrigation penalties in state Supreme Court
content: Ron Fodé, a dedicated farmer from Washington State, is fighting against hefty penalties threatening his agricultural livelihood due to irrigation practices. The conflict arose in 2017 over water rights for his crops, leading to the Department of Ecology rejecting his irrigation assistance applications. This has resulted in penalties totaling $618,000.

title: Kelly Clarkson's ex's $2.9M Montana ranch listed months after his death
content: Kelly Clarkson's late ex-husband Brandon Blackstock's 40-acre Montana estate has been listed for $2.9 million, less than a year after his death from cancer in August 2025. The 6,400-square-foot lodge features an indoor pool, spa, and equestrian facilities, reflecting Blackstock's love for the cowboy lifestyle he embraced after his divorce from Clarkson.

title: Woman's 'broken porcelain' in attic sells for £160k after 20 years
content: A woman in Lincolnshire rediscovered a box of inherited Chinese porcelain in her attic after twenty years. She inherited the pieces from her grandfather, Brigadier Robert Kellie, who collected them in China. After taking them to an auction house, the porcelain pieces were appraised and auctioned. Many items sold for much higher than expected, including one lot that fetched £59,000.

title: Before radar, Britain tried to hear enemy bombers coming using giant concrete ‘ears’
content: Britain’s Denge Sound Mirrors, three concrete structures on the Kent coast built between 1928 and 1930, were designed to catch the drone of approaching bombers and give defenders a few extra minutes of warning. Led by physicist Dr William Sansome Tucker, the project followed heavy World War 1 air raids on coastal towns. Faster aircraft, background noise and the arrival of radar made the mirrors obsolete by 1939.

title: Indian-American teen recycles 160,000 tennis balls into nonprofit success
content: Prem Kamasani, a high school student, started BallBack to recycle discarded tennis balls effectively. The organization provides collection bins to various sports facilities akin to schools and clubs. Volunteers collect the balls and partner with recycling organizations to repurpose or recycle them. BallBack has expanded across 16 states with over 310 members working towards sustainability. A world-record attempt for recycling tennis balls is planned for the future.

title: Bismack Biyombo’s $1.3M donation: How did his father inspire his Congo hospital project?
content: Bismack Biyombo, after losing his father to COVID-19, decided to donate his entire NBA salary to support healthcare. His commitment aims to build a hospital in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, naming it after his father. This decision reflects Biyombo's desire to improve medical access for families facing financial challenges. He has previously engaged in community projects through his foundation, furthering healthcare and educational initiatives.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he translated English for Messi at award ceremonies
content: Cristiano Ronaldo has opened up about his 15-year rivalry with Lionel Messi, revealing how he helped the Argentine understand English during award ceremonies. The Al-Nassr star described their relationship as respectful and their competition as healthy, comparing it to Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost. However, Ronaldo remains firm in his belief that his remarkable goalscoring record makes him football’s greatest ever.

title: He gave land given for road, sold TDRs for Rs 6.02 crore; ITAT taxes capital gains
content: The landowner chose to sell the TDRs he had received for surrendering 2,839 square metres of land. He sold them to a builder for Rs 6 crore but did not pay income tax on the proceeds. His understanding was that the amount received from the sale was a capital receipt and was therefore not taxable.

title: Kerala crash: Old video shows accused teen’s Mini Cooper speeding at 220kmph
content: Suhail Sajeev, a 19-year-old, was arrested after a crash in Nedumbassery that killed three people. The victims were returning home on a scooter when a Mini Cooper struck them from behind. Sajeev's Instagram video showed reckless driving, with a speedometer reaching 220kmph prior to the incident. Police suspect he was intoxicated during the accident, with ongoing investigations. Further inquiries into alcohol service by local bars are also being conducted.

title: SBI Research recommends LTCG on equities to be scrapped; calls for DTAA clarity
content: The proposal is aimed at making foreign capital flows into equities more stable and limiting the chances of abrupt withdrawals that could put pressure on the rupee. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) currently face a 12.5% LTCG tax on equity investments. The Union Budget 2026 retained this rate for listed shares and equity mutual funds, continuing the tax framework introduced as part of a major fiscal overhaul in 2024.

title: Bank cut Rs 5.89 crore FD rate from 7.75% to 3.5%; Court orders higher interest
content: Initially, the FD earned interest at rates of 7.75%, 8.25% and 7.75% over different periods. However, from January 30, 2018, the bank lowered the rate to 3.5%. Challenging the reduction, the deposit holder approached the court again, arguing that the bank had cut the interest rate without any valid reason or justification.

title: 'Disclose EC files, set up audit panel': Key points from INDIA bloc's plea in SC
content: A march led by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders reached the Supreme Court to contest electoral irregularities. The leaders filed a joint petition naming the Election Commission of India as a respondent. This petition challenges decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The opposition demands transparency and safeguards against voter deletions during the process.

title: Mohanlal praises Ajay Devgn's 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion': 'I am truly impressed'
content: After viewing 'Drishyam: The Conclusion', Mohanlal has lauded its fresh narrative, which sets it apart from the Malayalam versions. Starring Ajay Devgn as the cunning Vijay Salgaonkar, the film showcases his brilliant tactics against law enforcement. Impressively, it has grossed over Rs 479.80 crore worldwide since launch, with Jaideep Ahlawat's role introducing compelling new dynamics into the gripping plot.

title: Alexander Zverev crowned year-end world No. 1 after Alcaraz's shock Shanghai Masters defeat
content: Alexander Zverev has made history by clinching the year-end world No. 1 ranking for the very first time. His remarkable journey to the top was amplified by Carlos Alcaraz's surprising defeat at the Shanghai Masters. Zverev's stellar season includes his inaugural Grand Slam triumphs at both the French Open and US Open.

title: Demolition of tribals’ houses in M.P. draws Shivraj’s anger; says ‘Mohan ji became CM with their votes’

title: Magnitude 6 earthquake strikes off Panama
content:
A magnitude 6 earthquake struck Panama on Monday, following two powerful quakes that jolted the country's southern coast on Friday. According to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC), the quake was at a depth of 35 km. Panama recorded more than 300 aftershocks following Friday's magnitude 7.7 earthquake that damaged hundreds of homes and infrastructure across the country's central provinces, prompting the government to declare a national state of emergency over the weekend. No deaths were reported, but at least 27 people were injured and nearly 900 homes were damaged, according to emergency authorities, who warned the toll could rise as assessments continue in remote communities. Among the most affected provinces are Los Santos, Cocle, Veraguas, and Herrera, authorities added. (More details awaited)

title: Jantar Mantar out as protest hub; 3 new venues named
content: a ministry of home affairs committee set up to identify suitable venues for citizens to exercise their right to protest . the protests never took place inside the 18th-century, ASI-protected astronomical observatory . they were held on the adjoining Jantar Mantar Road, the starting point of many historic movements .

title: 60% of 33 lakh who received SIR notices in Delhi are now verified
content: over 60% of the 33 lakh voters who got notices in Delhi have been verified . more than 19 lakh voters were flagged for "logical discrepancies" nearly 14 lakh were classified as "unmapped" because their records could not be linked to the 2002 SIR .

title: As Jantar Mantar loses protest site tag, CJP plans get disrupted
content: police announced the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site . the force had 24 hours to set a date for its proposed protest against alleged electoral roll revision irregularities . police slammed the move, throwing the decision into uncertainty .

title: On cracker ban, SC says mustn't pass orders difficult to enforce
content: a bench of the amicus curiae and senior advocate said there could not be carte blanche for cracker bursting . the court refused to consider strict control over crackers and said the court must not pass orders which are difficult to implement on the ground . this came in response to a plea for a cracker ban which adversely affected the health of children, senior citizens and patients .
